claims.text: Replacing EAM reference potentials with machine-learning potentials will more accurately capture complex liquid configurations in multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting.
Using a machine-learning reference will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in thermodynamic integration.
The intended materials are near-equiatomic multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The method applies to solid or partially liquid states close to the alloys' high melting temperatures.
The proposed reference is a neural-network or other machine-learning interatomic potential fitted to ab initio configurations from both solid and liquid phases.
The training data should span the target compositional range.
The applicable systems contain four to six principal elements.
The applicable temperature interval is approximately 0.8–1.0 times the melting temperature or above.
Typical applicable temperatures are approximately 1500–3500 K, depending on composition.
A multi-element machine-learning potential can capture local bonding and coordination in both solid and liquid phases.
Capturing solid and liquid local environments reduces mismatch between the reference and ab initio potential-energy surfaces.
Broad high-temperature ab initio training provides comprehensive coverage of the relevant configurations.
Improved configuration coverage enables more faithful sampling of the liquid phase.
The machine-learning reference will produce smaller free-energy path differences than EAM references in thermodynamic integration.
The intervention will substantially reduce free-energy calculation error relative to EAM-based references.
The intervention will improve agreement with direct ab initio benchmarks for stability and melting transitions.
The relevant baseline is TOR–TILD using conventional EAM references for the same compositions.
Accuracy may fail outside the compositions and temperature–pressure regimes represented in the training data, or under extreme deformation and long-time dynamics.
Complete coverage of all relevant alloy configurations is challenging and requires additional ab initio data and cross-validation.
Failure to obtain a significantly smaller discrepancy from direct ab initio liquid free energies than with EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
